full_judgment:
4. In his writ petition the writ petitioner, (petitioner herein), stated that he filed an application for granting lease of Government khas land for the purpose of salt cultivation and subsequently Settlement Case No. 4 of 1984-1985 was started. The local Tahshilder duly held enquiry and submitted a report stating that out of 82 acres of land .22 acres contained trees and recommended for leasing out the remaining 60 acres of land in favour of the petitioner. But in spite of such recommendation the Revenue Officer did not take any steps and as a result the petitioner filed Other Class Suit No. 186 of 1987 for declaration that he was entitled to get lease of the suit land in Settlement Case No. 4 of 1984-1985. The suit was decreed on 26.09.1.990 but no execution case had yet been filed nor was the decree executed. Thereafter the petitioner again filed an application on 19.09.1997 but, there was no response. The petitioner came to know that the writ respondents were trying to lease out the land in favour of the writ respondent No. 8 on the direction of the Hon'ble Deputy Minister. (in-charge) of land; that after hearing such information the writ petitioner collected a copy of the said .application filed by the writ respondent No. 8, and found that he had filed the application to the Minister concerned in violation of the Labon Mohal Policy; that it appears from the said application that the Deputy Minister on receiving the said application directed the Secretary in the following manner “প্রস্তাব আকারে প্রতিবেদন সহ মন্ত্রণালয় চেয়ে পাঠান”; that subsequently on the basis of the above instruction of the Deputy Minister the writ respondent No. 2 by sending the said application asked the writ respondent No. 4 to send a proposal to the Minister; that the writ petitioner filed an application on 12.12.2005 against the action of the writ respondents for leasing out of the same to the writ respondent No. 8; that the writ petitioner also filed an application to the committee for leasing out the land in question in his favour as per the provision of the Labon Mohal Policy; that on 27.12.2005 the 2nd meeting of the Committee was held, and decision was taken to forward the recommendation to the Government for granting lease in favour of the writ respondent No. 8 and so far as it relates to the writ petitioner's objection they took a decision for making an enquiry into the objection of the writ petitioner; that to give final approval of the decision of the Meeting dated 27.12.2005, the writ respondent No. 4 sent the same to the writ respondent No. 1 for approval and for other, necessary steps; that the writ petitioner filed a petition to the Deputy Minister, Ministry of Land for getting lease of 60 acres of land in view of the judgment and decree passed in Other Suit No. 186 of 1987 of Mouza Saral and Gandamara and P.S. Banskhali of District Chittagong; that thereafter the writ respondent No. 2 sent a letter on 14.02.2006 to the writ respondent No. 4 stating that the proposed char land is out of survey and the same has not been declared as Labon Mohal and as such the proposal for leasing out the said land cannot be considered and also further directed to take step for declaring the same as Labon Mohal; that thereafter the writ respondent No. 4 issued a notice to the members of District Salt Development and Management Committee on 27.03.2006 for attending in a meeting held on 10.04.2006 incorporating 6 agendas to be discussed in the meeting. Out of the 6 agendas 3 agendas have been mentioned in respect of the writ petitioner; that the writ petitioner applied to the writ respondent No. 1 on 01.02.2006 for leasing out 60 acres of khas land and not to lease out the same in favour of so-called Upakulio Bahumukhi Samabaya Samity Limited and on the said application the Hon'ble Minister marked the same to the writ respondent No. 1 to stay all proceedings and to direct the writ respondent No. 4 for sending report with proposal to lease out the 60 acres of land in favour of the writ petitioner; that in view of the direction of the Hon'ble Minister of the Ministry of land the writ respondent No. 2 issued a letter to the writ respondent No. 4 on 15.02.2006 to take step in respect of the possession of the writ petitioner of the proposed land on inquiry into the matter that as per the notice a meeting of District Salt Development and Management Committee was held on 10.04.2006 which has been chaired by the writ respondent No. 4. In the said meeting the proposed land was declared as "Labon Mohal" in violation of section 3 of Labon Mohal Policy; that thereafter in view of the decision of meeting dated 10.04.2006 proposal was sent to the Ministry by the writ respondent No. 4 for final approval to lease out 108.74 acres of land to the writ respondent No. 8. The writ petitioner impugned the said letter dated 07.05.2006 in the writ petition. 

 9. Mr. Kamal-ul-Alam, the learned Senior Counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the procedure for leasing out any land for salt cultivation is contained in লবন মহাল ব্যবস্থাপনা নীতিমালা which was issued in the form of a circular dated 30.03.1992. He further submits that according to the Nitimala an application for lease has to be made to the Deputy Commissioner and the petitioner had made his application accordingly. The respondent No. 8 did not file any such application in accordance with the লবন মহাল ব্যবস্থাপনা নীতিমালা but directly filed his application before the Deputy Minister, Ministry of Land, Government of Bangladesh and the জেলা লবন সম্পদ উন্নয়ন ও ব্যবস্থাপনা সংক্রান্ত কমিটি took decision to lease out the land on the basis of such unlawful application. He also submits that the High Court Division erred in law in not considering the requirement of the Nitimala. He next submits that the respondent No. 8 filed his application for lease of the khas land in contravention of the Nitimala and the authorities concerned have failed to respond to the petitioner's objection against such unlawful application of the respondent No. 8. He finally submits that the লবন মহাল ব্যবস্থাপনা নীতিমালা contains the authority's guidelines for leasing out the government khas land, and the petitioner having filed his application in accordance with the provisions of the Nitimala has the right to be treated in accordance with those provisions. He submits that the High Court Division wrongly interpreted the provisions of the লবন মহাল ব্যবস্থাপনা নীতিমালা thereby misdirected itself in holding that the petitioner is not an aggrieved person and has no locus standi to claim lease for 60 acres of land. 

 III. For that having regard to the fact that the petitioner being an applicant for getting lease of লবন মহাল has a right to be treated in accordance with law of লবন মহাল ব্যবস্থাপনা নীতিমালা and having regard to the fact that under the provision of Clause 4(Gha) of the লবন মহাল ব্যবস্থাপনা নীতিমালা  the Ministry has been given discretionary power to grant lease of the Government khas land over a maximum of 15 acres of land in case the proposed লবন মহাল project is found to be financially and technically fit and that there is no bar for a Chairman to get lease for a লবন মহাল, the High Court Division, misinterpreted the provision of the লবন মহাল ব্যবস্থাপনা নীতিমালা and thereby misdirected itself in holding that the petitioner is not an aggrieved person and that a person can not a lease for maximum of land and that the petitioner being the Chairman and owner of land has no locus standi to claim lease for 60 acres of land".
